newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish MP quits conservative party, boosts Yilmaz.
newsitem.headline: Turkish MP quits conservative party, boosts Yilmaz.

text.p: A Turkish MP quit conservative Tansu Ciller's True Path Party on Sunday, boosting secularist prime minister-designate Mesut Yilmaz's chances of forming an anti-Islamist government.
NTV television said deputy Haluk Muftuler's resignation had reached the parliamentary speaker's office in the early hours of the morning.
The resignation reduced the number of MPs in a pro-Islamic alliance backed by Ciller to 281.
Yilmaz, appointed on Friday to try to replace fallen Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, can count on a maximum of 266 seats in his attempt to win a vote of confidence in any coalition he formed.
He would need the support of anti-Islamist dissidents in Ciller's party to carry the vote. Motherland Party leader Yilmaz has said he hopes to have a cabinet list by the end of June.
Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, stepped down last week after months of pressure from the secularist army.
